title: Why Teacher Calmness Equals Better Behavior
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin makes the case that maintaining a consistently calm disposition is one of the simplest changes a teacher can make with an outsized payoff, producing what he calls 'What the heck?' moments of surprising improvement. He walks through five specific effects of calmness: reduced excitability (since students take behavioral cues from the teacher), improved focus (because pacing, fast talk, and nervous energy pull student attention away from instruction), increased happiness that becomes contagious even with the hardest students, greater teacher confidence as slowing down creates more room to observe and prepare students for independence, and dramatically reduced stress. The concrete technique for achieving this state is what he calls the 'decide-first method,' paired with slowing physical pace, talking less, and breathing from the diaphragm, on the theory that calmness becomes automatic once a teacher commits to a classroom management plan that removes the need to react emotionally to misbehavior.
points: Calmness is contagious: even a class's most difficult student will start to relax and smile in response to a teacher's steady demeanor.
Simple physical adjustments -- slowing down, talking less, and breathing from the diaphragm -- visibly improve student focus.
Slowing your own pace creates more space to observe and model, which builds student confidence and independence over time.
The 'decide-first method' is the specific technique Linsin credits for making calmness a repeatable, teachable skill rather than a fixed personality trait.
quotes: Maintaining a calm disposition is one of those things. If you do nothing else, if you make no other changes to your teaching practice, you’ll notice some surprising effects.
As long as you allow your classroom management plan to take care of misbehavior for you, your calmness will pervade your classroom and soothe every restless spirit.
Simply slowing down, talking less, and breathing with your diaphragm will better draw your students’ eyes and energy toward you and your instruction.
It's all powerfully and predictably contagious. Even the hardest nut begins to smile in spite of himself.
I also recommend the decide-first method, which was a game-changer for me and thousands of other teachers.
Finally, adopting the SCM approach in full will make transitioning to a calm, confident teacher almost automatic.
